title: Publish Known Issues & Workarounds hub (landing + tags + initial articles)
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Internal docs: Adds a Known Issues & Workarounds hub with tags/filters and publishes the first batch of workaround articles. Intended to be linked from Support workflows and SDK troubleshooting sections.
body:
## Summary
This PR publishes a first-class **Known Issues & Workarounds** hub on redwood-docs and ships the initial batch of workaround articles validated during the Support “known-issues sprint”.

The goal is to reduce time-to-mitigation and repeat tickets by making workarounds discoverable, copy/paste-ready, and consistently linkable from Support macros + Jira.

## What’s included
- New landing page: **/support/known-issues**
  - Lightweight tag system (region / tier / surface / model)
  - “When to escalate” callout pattern
  - Clear recency + owner / last-reviewed metadata
- New article templates (frontmatter + structure) to standardize known-issues content
  - Required sections: Symptoms, Impact, Affected, Workaround, Validation, When to escalate, References
  - Prominent reminder: do not include customer-identifying details
- Initial workaround articles published:
  - Streaming timeouts / disconnects + reconnect guidance
  - 429 quota mismatch + interpreting rate-limit headers
  - Dedicated autoscaling oscillation (mitigations + knobs)
  - Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations (rollback + artifacts)
  - Audit log delivery latency (expectations + mitigations)

## Why now
Support escalation volume for these themes has been high in Q1 and we’re seeing repeated “same question” threads across accounts. Publishing validated workarounds in a consistent format lets Support and CS:
- Link the same answer everywhere (ticket, Slack bridge, email)
- Reduce back-and-forth for diagnostics
- Standardize escalation triggers and expectations

## Design/IA notes
- Layout follows DES-233 guidance: scannable cards, filters, and explicit escalation callouts.
- Tags are intentionally small + constrained to avoid taxonomy sprawl.

## Safety / sensitivity
- No customer names, request IDs, or screenshots with identifiable info.
- Articles link to internal runbooks only when they’re in Support-safe Confluence; otherwise use generic instructions.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)
- ENG-4826: Connect hub into broader help center nav + add cross-links from SDK troubleshooting
- ENG-4823: Add “Support-safe quick view” dashboards and link them consistently in articles
- ENG-4822/ENG-4825: As runtime/gateway fixes roll out, update the affected-versions sections and adjust language from workaround → resolved

## Testing
- `pnpm test` (docs)
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm build` + link check

## Screenshots
- Landing page + filters (see PR attachments)
- Example article page (streaming disconnect)

Refs: Support sprint plan + publication criteria (PM-913).

review_conversation:
Dev Patel: Please make sure every article has a clear “When to escalate” section and that the first paragraph is copy/paste-able into a ticket. Also avoid any language that implies we’ll always provide credits.
Elliot Price: Updated all five articles to include a standard “When to escalate” section and tightened the first paragraph into a customer-safe summary. Removed the credits language and linked to the separate policy doc where relevant.

Priya Shah: The landing page needs tags for tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and region, otherwise Support can’t quickly narrow during triage. Also we should include a “Last reviewed” date.
Elliot Price: Added tier + region tags to frontmatter, implemented filters, and added `last_reviewed` field surfaced on cards + page header. Also added a short tag glossary in the authoring notes.

Wei Chen: Streaming article: please avoid recommending disabling HTTP/2 as a blanket fix; frame it as “if you see X and you control the proxy”. Also add a short snippet for idempotency/retry and call out request ID logging.
Elliot Price: Adjusted wording to conditional guidance, added retry/idempotency snippet, and included “capture request_id” guidance with a link target for SDK troubleshooting follow-up (ENG-4827).

Kira Thompson: Private installer article: remove any cluster log examples that mention customer namespaces; keep artifacts list but generic. Also add explicit escalation path to Private Deployments / Platform.
Elliot Price: Scrubbed log examples, kept artifact checklist generic, and added escalation path section with ownership boundaries. Added a reminder callout about handling logs securely.

Owen Phillips: Suggest making the hub URL stable and short; Support macros will link to it. Also ensure the index is easy to scan on mobile.
Elliot Price: Locked the URL as `/support/known-issues` and added a redirect alias from the longer path. Adjusted card spacing and tag wrapping for narrow widths.
post_merge_notes: After merge, Support macros should point to the hub and specific article anchors. Docs team to monitor search queries + ticket deflection for 2 weeks and iterate on tag naming if needed.
